review.publication: Local only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: Calendar systems, representations, civil periods and scheduling; split Wednesday from environment and correct Sunday and schedule senses.
review.attribution: Reviewed adaptations of Open English WordNet 2025 by the Open English WordNet Team, derived from Princeton WordNet. CC BY 4.0 and Princeton notices remain in docs/quality/2026-10-09-q11.md#sources-and-reuse. Russian labels and graph mappings are adaptations. USNO supports calendar distinctions; NIST and RFC date/calendar documentation support separating local civil dates, duration and representations. No implementation of a calendar standard is claimed.
review.context_policy: All new concepts and assertions use U1 with unspecified strength. Existing home contexts and relation grammar remain unchanged. Calendar formats are general information objects, not software implementations.

sense_decisions.scope: The weekday between Tuesday and Thursday. Do not import an ordinal position or claim that it is always a working day.
Rules organizing named calendar periods and dates. Separate the abstract system from a printed or electronic calendar representation.
A calendar whose annual structure follows the seasonal solar cycle. Do not conflate its month names with lunar phases.
A calendar organized around lunar cycles; selected here as the lunar calendar family distinguished from lunisolar calendars.
A calendar coordinating lunar months with the solar year. Do not automatically place it under the separately scoped purely lunar family.
The Gregorian solar-calendar system. Its leap-year rule is supported by USNO; numerical rules are documented in the source, not encoded as guessed graph attributes.
The Julian solar-calendar system, distinct from a Julian date (continuous astronomical day count).
A tabular representation of calendar dates. Select the informational table, not its paper, screen, a system of rules or a list of appointments.
A reusable chart relating dates and weekdays across years. Restrict the dictionary chart-or-device meaning to the chart; a watch mechanism is not a table.
An informational designation of a day in a specified calendar, distinct from the elapsed day, a date fruit, a romantic meeting or a single instant with a time zone.
A local civil day reckoned from midnight to the next midnight. Do not force it under the fixed 24-hour unit: clock changes can alter elapsed duration.
A complete annual cycle as defined by a calendar. Broaden the dictionary Gregorian-only gloss; January 1 and 365/366 days apply only after a calendar is specified.
A January-to-December year in the Gregorian calendar; distinguish it from a tropical year and other calendar years.
A Gregorian year including February 29. Do not infer that every calendar leap year has 366 days or uses February.
A Gregorian year without the intercalated February day. It is not the generic duration of every year.
The additional civil day in a Gregorian leap year. This is a day type, not the whole leap year or the act of intercalation.
A named month in a calendar. Do not fix its elapsed length to 30 days or require all calendar systems to have exactly twelve months.
A period of two consecutive weeks. Do not confuse it with half of a calendar month.
A civil day on which work is done for the relevant worker or activity. Do not import weekday as a universal genus: weekend work also exists.
A day on which the relevant person is not required to work. No universal Saturday/Sunday pattern or legal rule is asserted.
A specified latest time for completing something. Separate the time point from term 5166, which denotes an interval, and do not assert legal consequences.
Planning the order and time of activities. The result is a schedule, not the actual occurrence of the activities; software-programming synonyms are excluded.
A schedule of intended transport arrivals and departures. The plan does not guarantee actual punctuality.
A schedule of instructional sessions; not a school year, an attendance register or a legal attendance obligation.
A schedule recording planned appointments. Restrict the dictionary event-register sense; distinguish it from a calendar system and a date table.
An informational calendar entry that records a date for an event or activity. The entry is not the event itself.
A social meeting arranged in advance. Exclude appointment to a job, the appointee, equipment and the separate legal-disposition sense.
The annual period of an educational program. Do not identify it with January through December or a fixed 365-day duration.
Keep the spatial-surroundings record; its fifteen environment adjectives need their own sense review, but none may remain a weekday descendant.
Correct Sunday spelling without declaring the separate valid word for resurrection nonexistent. Generated resurrection record 10574 remains deferred.
Reuse and reparent schedule rather than duplicate its normal Russian spelling.
Keep term as a period; add deadline as a distinct time point.
Retain the broader month record and refine named calendar months through a nearer family.
Birthday can also be an anniversary; do not import the dictionary anniversary synonym onto the existing jubilee record without reviewing the conflicting exclusion.
Existing jubilee is narrower than every anniversary; broader anniversary-date and celebration senses remain deferred.
Keep the existing romantic-date record separate from the newly arranged-meeting and calendar-date senses.
Weekday has varying Saturday conventions; do not use it as the universal genus of working day.
The dictionary weekend assumes a Sunday-containing period. Weekend patterns remain deferred rather than imported globally.
The dictionary time-zone gloss assumes 24 regions. Time-zone rules and offsets require a separate qualified review.
Clock midnight and a unique global instant require date and zone distinctions; no unqualified time-point import.
A date fruit is not a calendar date.
The equinox gloss equates day and night lengths; astronomical and observational distinctions need a separate source review.

review.limits: No universal first weekday, weekend pattern, fixed UTC offset, calendar-day length, legal deadline or school-year duration is asserted. Calendar conventions and scheduling do not imply that an event actually occurred. Temporal part-whole links (month contains days; year contains months or leap day) are not encoded because the current relation-20 object signature excludes time periods; no incorrect genus or causal replacement is used. Environment adjective descendants, resurrection senses, birthday/anniversary overlap, decade/count mix-ups and remaining upper-graph conflicts require separate review. No application test suites.

exclusion_review.decision: Keep the time/space exclusion and resolve its Wednesday/environment homonym witness through a sense split. No new conflict or witness may appear.

review.collision_decision: Wednesday moves off 3515; the ambiguous Russian lookup sreda remains on both explicitly qualified senses. No other existing term collision is allowed.

refreshed_comparison.caveat: Normalized English spelling candidates are not verified identities or missing-concept counts.
